Here's what Boeing reported for the third quarter compared with what Wall Street analysts are expected, according to consensus estimates from LSEG: Loss per share: 34 cents adjusted vs. a loss of 21 cents expected Revenue: $24.19 billion expected vs $23.84 billion expected. For the three months ended Sept. 30, Boeing reported a net loss of $116 million, or 26 cents a share, compared with a $5.34 billion loss, or $7.14 per share, a year earlier. Adjusting for one-time items, the company reported a loss of 34 cents a share. A year earlier, Boeing had taken a nearly $5 billion charge on its long-delayed 777X aircraft program. Revenue climbed 4% on the year to $24.19 billion. Free cash flow rose to $464 million from $238 million in the third quarter of 2025. The company's defense unit revenue rose 15% in the third quarter from a year earlier to $7.94 billion. Boeing delivered 161 commercial airplanes in the third quarter, one more jet than a year earlier. Revenue in the all-important commercial aircraft business fell 3% to $10.72 billion. The unit had a negative operating margin of 6.5% because of a "less favorable delivery mix, higher projected costs associated with future production rate adjustments and higher estimated supply chain costs," Boeing said. The plane manufacturer's executives are set to update investors on how quickly it can increase aircraft production in the coming months when it holds a quarterly earnings call on Tuesday at 10:30 a.m. ET. Boeing has been producing about 47 of its 737 Max planes a month, but is aiming for more. CEO Kelly Ortberg told investors last month that production is taking "a little bit longer" than expected to stabilize, and the company expects to increase its output of the planes next year. "Looking ahead, expectations are rising, and they should," Ortberg said in a note to staff on Tuesday. "That means elevating our performance through lean, productivity and efficiency improvements in our day-to-day work while upholding our high levels of safety and quality." Aircraft production and deliveries are key to Boeing's recovery since the bulk of an aircraft's price is paid when the customer receives it. But the manufacturer had some wins lately. The U.S. Navy tapped Boeing to develop its next-generation fighter jet. And the Federal Aviation Administration last week signed off on the 737 Max 10 , the largest in the Max family. For the full year, Coke now expects comparable earnings per share to grow at least 11%, up from its prior forecast of an increase in the range of 9% to 10%. The beverage giant also anticipates that its organic revenue will climb at least 5%, a slight increase from its previous outlook of approximately 5% growth. The company's unit case volume increased 5%, helped by higher demand outside of North America. Coke's home market reported flat volume. In recent quarters, Coke executives have said North American shoppers are under pressure, stretched thin by inflation and economic uncertainty. But the beverage giant has also said consumers are still buying its drinks, from premium brands like Fairlife to its namesake soda. Globally, Coke's sparkling soft drinks business saw volume increase 5% during the quarter, lifted by growth of Coke, Coke Zero Sugar and Diet Coke. Coke's water, sports, coffee and tea division also saw volume climb by 5%. Increased demand for its water, which includes its premium Smartwater brand, fueled the growth. headlines.article_text: GM will switch to Nasdaq from the NYSE on Nov. 17 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points General Motors plans to transfer its common-stock listing from the New York Stock Exchange to Nasdaq, with trading expected to begin Nov. 17. The automaker expects to keep its “GM” ticker symbol, and the company says shareholders do not need to take action because of the transfer. The transfer would make GM eligible for potential inclusion in the Nasdaq-100 Index, while aligning the listing with GM’s technology-driven strategy. In this article GM NDAQ Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:06 01:06 GM to move from NYSE to Nasdaq Squawk Box DETROIT — General Motors plans to transfer shares of its common stock from the New York Stock Exchange to the Nasdaq as the automaker attempts to position itself more as a technology-focused company. The Detroit automaker said Tuesday that it expects to begin trading as a Nasdaq -listed company on Nov. 17. Its ticker symbol is expected to remain "GM," the company said. "GM's customer-focused, technology-driven strategy is creating value for our stockholders, making Nasdaq a natural home for our listing as we grow," GM CFO Paul Jacobson said in a release. "We're grateful for our long-standing partnership with the New York Stock Exchange and its remarkable legacy." GM noted the move will provide eligibility for potential inclusion in the Nasdaq-100 Index . Current shareholders do not need to take any action with respect to the transfer, the company said. The switch marks a notable loss for the NYSE, as GM first listed on the exchange in 1911. The Detroit automaker also relisted on the stock exchange in 2010 following a government-backed bankruptcy. General Motors vs. Ford Motor stock GM follows other companies such as Walmart , DoorDash and Palantir Technologies that have transferred from the more traditional NYSE to the historically technology focused Nasdaq in recent years. Hilton Worldwide Holdings last week also announced plans to move trading from the NYSE to Nasdaq. The key drivers for a listing transfer differ from company to company, but the Nasdaq in 2024 said common reasons include "index inclusion opportunities, cost effective fee structure, brand visibility partnership, access to Nasdaq's event space, and Nasdaq's suite of investor relations and ESG products." GM's decision comes a week after the automaker held a technology-focused event where executives laid out the company's roadmap for artificial intelligence and self-driving vehicle technologies. Shares of GM, which has been aggressively buying back stock , have more than doubled since 2024. GM's stock closed Monday at $76.31 per share. The company's market cap is roughly $64.4 billion.
